findings.condition: The contract (inputs/requirements.txt) requires J1 pin 2 = input and pin 1 = filtered output. In the saved schematic and board, J1 pin 1 connects to the raw input node /IN (with R1 pin 1) and J1 pin 2 connects to the filtered R1/C1 node /OUT (with R1 pin 2 and C1 pin 1). Pin 3 = GND is correct. Confirmed by independent kicad-cli netlist re-export and by geometric pin-position derivation: with the 180-degree instance transform, J1 pin 1 lands at (66.04, 66.04) on the wire labeled IN and pin 2 at (66.04, 63.50) on the wire labeled OUT; PCB pad nets and DRC parity (0 issues) show the board inherits the same assignment.

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch (symbol J1 uuid 465541a7-d06f-5282-b75f-15b79e4182a2 at 60.96,63.5 rot 180; labels IN at 68.58,66.04 and OUT at 68.58,63.5) and inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb (J1 pads: pad 1 net /IN, pad 2 net /OUT)
findings.mechanism: A system honoring the contract drives pin 2 and takes the filtered output from pin 1. On this board that drives the C1 node directly and reads through the 10k resistor: ngspice AC analysis shows a flat ~-0.086 dB response from 10 Hz to 100 kHz into a 1 Megohm load (no low-pass behavior), while the 100 nF capacitor loads the source directly. The intended ~159 Hz low-pass (-16 dB at 1 kHz) only exists in the reverse, non-contract orientation. All toolchain checks (ERC, DRC, parity) pass because the schematic's internal IN/OUT labels are self-consistent with the wrong pin choice; the successful exits do not demonstrate contract conformance.
findings.reasoning: The scope's single criterion is conformance of saved connectivity to the external connector contract, and the saved design fails it: the input and filtered-output pins are interchanged in both the schematic and the board. Two independent derivations (netlist export and raw-coordinate pin mapping) agree, so this is not a tool artifact, and DRC parity of 0 confirms the board matches the swapped schematic. The clean ERC/DRC/netlist results are expected despite the defect because the error is in which physical pin each net reaches, not in internal consistency. Electrically the swap is not benign: used per the contract the circuit provides no filtering and presents the capacitor directly to the external driver. Because the design violates its only stated functional requirement at the external interface, severity is blocking and the assessment is defect.
findings.title: J1 pins 1 and 2 are swapped relative to the stated connector contract (input and filtered output inverted)

limitations: ngspice demonstration uses ideal R/C with a 1 Megohm load; no load impedance is stated in the operating conditions, so the contract-orientation result (no filtering into a high-impedance load) assumes a high-impedance measurement point
No ratings, tolerance, thermal, or EMC assessment performed: inputs/requirements.txt restricts evaluation to the stated connector contract and forbids imposing unstated ratings
Zone fill evaluated as saved; the read-only candidate forbids a refill pass, so zone connectivity relies on the saved filled_polygon plus DRC/geometry probe results

Stock symbol/footprint library files referenced by the project (KICAD10_* paths) were not independently audited beyond the lib_symbols embedded in the schematic and the footprints embedded in the board
Physical mating-connector fit and real connector part verification are out of scope; J1 is a generic 2.54 mm pin header
